main_text.p: sæle, unde nostrum South. Belg. etiam Auster Sapden-wotnd: Germ. Sud-wotnt.

Farlt, Princeps: & forlstingo, præpositione: nos wɔzst] Ab eâdem origine nostratium stst, (adjectivum) Primus, & adverb. stst, primùm, vel in primis. Plura vide apud Cl. Selden. nostr. Tit. Honor. par. 2. cap. 1. §. 53. & Versteg. cap. 10.
Furtteltin, Prodigium: nos wɔzs-tecken] Hoc Sax. pope tacn, & pope beacn. A priori, nostrum tozetoken, voce compositâ à pope, præ, & tacn, nobis token, signum.
main_text.head: Verba.
main_text.p: Farlifbon, Transierunt: farlief, transeat] Transire, Sax. papan: unde fare in nostratium twarre-fare, Saxon. pynopape, alias utpape, id est, expeditio. Hinc etiam viatorem vocamus Map-farting-man, Sax. pezpepenb: Mari versatum, ut Nautam, sea-farting-man:

page.notes: Marginal marks and handwritten numerals at the right edge are not printed text. Several words in Old English/Saxon and Dutch/German glosses are in black letter and are transcribed as best read; the Saxon forms are uncertain and marked by approximation only where doubtful.
